headline: Cohere makes initial close of Series E round targeting up to $7 billion Canadian dollars
body: Cohere announced the initial close of a Series E round targeting up to $7 billion Canadian dollars (about $5 billion), in a post that rejects what it calls frontier fatalism. Bloomberg reported that the round values Cohere at $20.5 billion, and that the Canadian government has agreed to invest up to $1.14 billion.
note: For banks weighing where their models come from, Cohere's pitch is a platform that lets institutions own the AI they run on, the company says.

evidence.text: Canadian artificial intelligence company Cohere said in a Thursday (Oct. 29) company blog post that it rejects what it called “ frontier fatalism .”

That’s its term for the belief that AI will be monopolized by a handful of United States and Chinese tech giants. To offer other countries a sovereign alternative, Cohere announced in the post the initial close of a Series E funding round targeting up to $7 billion Canadian dollars (about $5 billion).
The funding values Cohere at $20.5 billion, roughly triple its value from last year.

The Canadian government has agreed to invest up to $1.14 billion in Cohere, while the company plans to remain based in Canada and invest around $1.2 billion in new computing infrastructure in the country by 2030, Bloomberg reported Thursday.
“Our ambition is to build frontier models that compete with the best in the world, a secure platform that lets institutions own the AI they run on, and cyber defenses democracies can rely on.
